claims.claim: young white perch in the Hudson River grew 0.33–0.74 mm/d (field, juveniles)
claims.location: p. 55 (PDF p. 70), Table 1.7; Fig. 1.10, p. 68 (PDF p. 83); methods p. 23 (PDF p. 38)
claims.conditions: slopes of ANCOVA length-on-age regressions (length mm, otolith age in days) for young-of-year aged ~70–155 d from the NYSDEC fall seine survey (Aug–early Oct); 2013 year class n = 67 (45 resident, 22 migratory), 2014 n = 57 (29/28); slopes 0.33 (2013 resident), 0.67 (2013 migratory), 0.68 (2014 resident), 0.74 (2014 migratory) — 'late-juvenile growth rates'
claims.note: Read on the page image of Table 1.7 and the axes of Fig. 1.10 (Length (mm) vs Age (days)). Two year classes only; the low 0.33 is the resident contingent in the high-flow 2013.

claims.claim: Hudson young white perch were larger in warm summers and smaller after dense larval years
claims.quote: positively associated with mean summer water temperature (r = 0.70; p < 0.01)
claims.conditions: Pearson correlations over 1992–2013 of the annual mean October total length (river-wide utilities' beach seine survey) with mean summer temperature (r = 0.70), summer flow (r = −0.50) and the post-yolk-sac larval standing stock (r = −0.46, p < 0.05)
claims.note: Correlations, not experiments; 'dense larval years' = the PYSL standing stock of the same year.

claims.claim: Hudson River white perch, 1992–2013: 73.9 mm (62.8–82.3) in October
claims.location: p. 112 (PDF p. 127), Table 2.2; definition p. 82 (PDF p. 97)
claims.quote: Mean YOY length in October … mm … 73.9 … 62.8 … 82.3
claims.conditions: mean, minimum and maximum of the annual means 1992–2013; each annual mean = the mean river-wide total length in the first and third weeks of October (weeks 40 and 42) of the utilities' beach seine survey (data ASA 2014)
claims.note: The layout text puts 'Unitless' beside this row; the page image shows the unit is mm (the units column drifts by a row in the text layer).

notes: Chapter 1 also gives back-calculated size at 50 days post-hatch (mean 20.5 mm in 2013 vs 33.5 mm in 2014, p. 34) and von Bertalanffy parameters for adults (migratory k = 0.69, L∞ = 204 mm; resident k = 0.52, L∞ = 194 mm, p. 31). This is an estuary (tidal Hudson), not a lake; the growth and size values are analogs only.
